I farm 90 mu, so I do not run it like a tiny household plot. I still count every yuan, but on this much land I cannot gamble with yield. I will start from what has worked for me before: keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation, and keep a smaller block for stevia because that crop takes more watching and more hand work. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect the wheat at jointing and grain filling, and to help maize at the key growth stages if the rain is short. With my schooling level, I do not talk too fancy, but I do look at the field carefully. If wheat is pale, I will not be stingy with nitrogen. If maize wants to push hard after the summer rain, I will topdress in time. Around here, if a man cuts fertilizer too much and misses yield, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on one more bag. I also watch what other good farmers nearby do, and the better-yielding fields usually do not starve the crop. For stevia, I will keep the area smaller and manage it tighter, because it can pay well but it needs cleaner fields and more careful spraying. I will use rotary tillage on most land because it is faster and cheaper for my size, and I can finish on time.
